#Miles Morales: The Ultimate Spider-Man As I pointed out in an [earlier post](https://voat.co/v/Marvel/comments/1081784), I was really blown away by it. I don't recall who recommended it to me, but thanks. It was an awesome and fun read, and I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys the Spider-Man franchise.

#Spider-Man (2016) So far, this has been very enjoyable, too. I'm especially stoked for the re-emergence of Black Cat, who's one of my favorites from the franchise. I have to admit, I was never really "into" Spider-Man (Peter Parker) as much as I was those who orbited around him; Black Cat, Venom, Scarlet Spider-- yes, I admit, I was one of the few(?) who found some enjoyment in the Clone Saga. At least, I thought the premise that Parker was the clone and Reilly was the "original" to be interesting and cool. The rest of it... eh... not so much.

Got to say, I want to see Miles square off against Venom or-- hell, I'd *love* to see how he would deal with Carnage.

#Mockingbird Bobbi in the comics is nothing like Bobbi on Agents of SHIELD, which is a real shame. Though there's been three issues, at it's best moments (issue #2), words like "passable," "junk-food", "superficial," and "filler" all come to mind in regards to the writing. At it's worst moments (issues #1 & #3), it was an absolute steaming pile of shit. If you bought it, take Geoff Johns up on his offer and get your money back.

As an aside, I really wish people who clearly lack any understanding or experience BDSM or alternative lifestyles would stop trying to write about those alternative lifestyles. But then, considering what the rest of the series gets wrong... like writing *every single female superhero out of Marvel history ever*... why the fuck am I surprised that Chelsea Cain would watch 50 Shades of Grey and think she was suddenly an expert in the subject matter?

Regardless, I might give one last shot to issue #4 when it comes out... but I don't see myself continuing the series past that without some serious editorial overhauling. Poor Bobbi must feel like shit, because Marvel seems to keep publishing her stories when she's on her period.

#Black Panther (2016) So far, I'm conflicted on this series. Its start has been a little rocky, but Coats' writing reflects common political attitudes toward Africa. It's interesting to see that he represents both the "women who survive their sons, husbands, brothers, and fathers are the REAL victims of war" and the "strong independent black woman don't need no man" attitudes in the same book. I'm hoping that this is intentional, and will eventually be subverted. But given Marvel's recent SJW bent...

#All-New All-Different Avengers This was another series with a rocky start. In its earlier issues, it had some casual racism against blacks AND whites thrown in "unironically." On top of it, the writing comes off at times as superficial and clearly aimed toward the broader segment of the Young-Adult market that's used to more "packaged" experiences. This is nowhere more obvious than in exchanges between Ms. Marvel (Kamala Khan) and Nova (Sam Alexander). At least Nova doesn't sparkle.

Fortunately, despite a few stumbles here and there, the series manages to stay pretty interesting. I'm going to continue reading.
